prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Houston for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” dentist for implants in Houston — the best provider for you depends on your specific needs (complexity of the case, bone loss, medical history), your insurance and budget, and whether you prefer an oral surgeon, periodontist, or prosthodontist. I can help you find top local options if you tell me your zip code or neighborhood and any preferences. Meanwhile, here’s how to find and choose the right implant specialist.

Who typically places implants
- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons (OMS): surgical placement, complex cases, sedation.
- Periodontists: surgical placement, bone-grafting expertise.
- Prosthodontists: focused on the restoration (crowns/bridges) and complex prosthetics.
- Many great practices use multidisciplinary teams (surgeon + prosthodontist).

What to look for
- Relevant specialty training and credentials (board certification, affiliation with AAOMS, AAP, AAID, ICOI, Academy of Osseointegration).
- Experience: number of implants placed and experience with cases like yours (e.g., sinus lift, full-arch).
- Technology: CBCT (3D imaging), guided-surgery planning, digital implant workflows.
- Before/after photos and patient testimonials.
- Clear pricing, treatment timeline, and follow-up plan.
- Willingness to handle complications and offer warranties/guarantees if appropriate.
- Good communication and clarity about alternatives (bridges, dentures, implants).

Questions to ask at a consult
- How many implants do you place per year? How many cases similar to mine?
- Are you a specialist? What training do you have in implants?
- Will you do the crown/restoration or coordinate with my restorative dentist?
- Do you use CBCT and guided implant planning?
- What are all the costs (implant + abutment + crown; grafts; follow-ups)?
- What are my options if bone or sinus grafting is required?
- Can I see before/after photos and get patient references?

How to find top candidates
- Ask your general dentist for a referral (they know who does consistently good restorations).
- Search review sites (Google, Yelp, Healthgrades, Zocdoc) and look for consistent recent reviews.
- Use professional directories: AAOMS (oral surgeons), American Academy of Periodontology, American Academy of Implant Dentistry.
- Check local dental schools/advanced clinics (UTHealth School of Dentistry may offer experienced faculty care at competitive prices).

Typical cost range (very approximate)
- Single implant (implant body + abutment + crown): roughly $2,000–$5,000+ depending on materials, location, and need for grafting. Complex cases (full-arch, sinus lifts) cost more.

If you want, tell me:
- Your Houston zip code or neighborhood
- Whether you have dental insurance or prefer a certain specialist type
- If you have complex issues (bone loss, medical conditions)

I can then look up highly rated implant specialists in your area and give a short list with contact info and what makes each a good option.
